> **This is a beta. Back up your files. Please report bugs.**
> Hindsight 1.0.0-beta.1 has been tested headlessly (125 automated tests on Blender 4.2 and 5.2) but not yet widely in the real Blender interface. Keep saving versions of important work, and tell us what breaks: https://github.com/Min3scon/Hindsight/issues/new/choose

## What it does
Hindsight gives every object its own scrubbable sculpt history of up to 10,000 steps, separate from Blender's undo.
- **Scrubber** along the bottom of the 3D Viewport with a step counter; the dot at its left opens the **History Menu**.
- **Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z** (Cmd on Mac) step through the history in Sculpt and Vertex Paint mode, alongside Blender's own undo.
- Records sculpt strokes, masks, Face Sets, visibility, vertex colours, filters, Voxel Remesh / Trim (full snapshots) and Edit Mode changes (one step when you leave Edit Mode).
- **Morph History brush**: set a morph target, then paint parts of the mesh back toward it.
- **Global history** with **Preserve Modes**, **Movie Mode** timelapse playback, **Join with unmerge**, Separate / duplicate handling, **Collection Filtering**.
- History is saved beside the .blend (Sidecar), inside it (Embed) or both, with crash recovery (Last Saved / Interrupted Session).

## Install
1. Download `hindsight.zip` below (or from https://min3scon.github.io/Hindsight/download/hindsight.zip).
2. In Blender 4.2 or newer: **Edit > Preferences > Get Extensions > Install from Disk**, pick the zip.
3. In the 3D Viewport press **N** and open the **Undo History** tab. Sculpt a stroke and the scrubber appears.

## What's tested
- 125 headless tests on Blender 4.2.23 and 5.2.2 (Blender's Python module): every recorded data type, bit-exact scrubbing after every jump, branching and truncation, Edit Mode grouping, topology snapshots, global history, Movie Mode keyframing, Morph History, join / unmerge / re-merge, separate and duplicate, collection filtering, save and reload in all three save modes, crash recovery, the 10,000-step cap and memory eviction.
- 10,000-step stress test on a 99.5k-vertex mesh (bit-exact jumps).
- The zip validates with Blender's extension builder and installs with Blender's own extension installer.

## Still needs real-Blender testing
- The on-screen scrubber: drawing, dragging (it must win over brush strokes), the History Menu dot.
- Brush stroke detection: exactly one step per real stroke, filter and mask/face-set operation; F9 tweaks.
- Viewport refresh after scrubbing in Sculpt Mode.
- Ctrl+Z interplay with Blender's native undo, and the confirmation dialogs.
- The Morph History tool in the Sculpt toolbar.

## Known issues
- A morph target is cleared if branching drops its step; set a new one.
- A stroke that exactly reverses the previous step bit-for-bit is treated as an undo.
- Movie Mode crossing a topology change while the object is in Sculpt Mode applies that step one tick late; render timelapses in Object Mode.
- A long pause in the middle of a stroke could split it into two steps.
- Not supported yet: Dyntopo, Multires. Object transforms, modifiers, shape keys, materials, vertex groups and weight paint are not stored. Blender's Global Undo must be enabled.

## Measured benchmarks
Headless, Blender 4.2 Python module, 4-core 2.1 GHz Xeon, strokes touching ~2% of the vertices (no viewport redraw included):

| | 100k vertices | 500k vertices |
|---|---|---|
| Memory per step (packed / raw) | 12.4 KB / 32.1 KB | 58.8 KB / 159.5 KB |
| Record a stroke | 1.07 ms | 3.58 ms |
| Scrub 1 / 100 / 300 steps | 0.39 / 13.0 / 36.3 ms | 1.51 / 55.8 / 161 ms |
| Save / load, 300 steps | 105 / 118 ms | 740 / 678 ms |

10,000 steps on 99.5k vertices: 25.8 MiB of history, about 0.95 ms per recorded stroke. 1M-vertex numbers are not measured yet.
